title: Draft: Win32: Make {Wire,Strato}shark console apps that don't allocate consoles
description:
Windows added an option for an "application that seems like a graphical
application when run from Explorer, but you can also write debug output
to the console, if run inside an existing console session." That's what
we want for Wireshark and Stratoshark - by default the logging system
opens a console when needed when not run from inside an existing console
session. There's also an advanced preference to always open the debug
console, or to never open it.

To do this, we make it a console subsystem application, and add an
appropriate entry to the application manifest. Note that this requires
Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100) or later, which includes Windows Server
2025. On earlier versions of Windows the XML entry is ignored, which
means that a console will always be opened. We also need to make sure
that the CLI applications that assume that a console exists and don't
always create one on demand use a different manifest. Otherwise, e.g.,
dumpcap will start up without creating a console and just run in the
background silently capturing packets and have to be quit via Task
Manager.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/console-allocation-policy

Fix #18137

notes.body: This works perfectly fine, it just makes the console always spawn on Windows 10 since the new manifest option was added in Windows 11, so we have to decide whether and when that's acceptable.

For Windows 10, we might be able to check if our process is the only one on the console ( https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20160125-00/?p=92922 ) and then call FreeConsole ( https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/freeconsole ) if so. (The Win32 API suggests that Raymond Chen's suggestion is slightly wrong in the sense that buffer cannot be `nullptr` even if you only want the count - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/getconsoleprocesslist .)
